messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Aisha Rao <aisha@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy onboarding — preflight questions and timelines

Marcus — thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached are our initial answers to the questionnaire (Acme_Preflight_Answers.pdf). A few follow-ups from our infra team: 

- We need a canonical checklist that our networking and security teams can sign off on (one-page playbook would be ideal).
- Timeline: we’re targeting a soft go‑live window Nov 18–20. What validation/acceptance tasks must be completed before that window?
- KMS: we will be bringing our customer‑managed key (AWS KMS). What are Redwood’s expectations for key rotation and audit evidence?

Can you send an intake checklist we can map to our internal milestones? Also sending our network diagram next.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Cloud Operations, Acme Health
attachments: Acme_Preflight_Answers.pdf (application/pdf, 312 KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy onboarding — preflight questions and timelines

Thanks Daniel — got the questionnaire. High level answers inline below and I’ve attached our intake checklist and recommended acceptance gates (redwood_onprem_onboarding_checklist.xlsx). Please review with your networking and security owners and come back with owners/timelines. 

Quick summary of must-have gates before soft go-live (Nov 18–20 target):
1) Network connectivity & routing validated (bastion, peering, egress, allowlist).
2) KMS integration completed and test encrypt/decrypt flows run against a sample workspace.
3) Service account IAM and RBAC mapping confirmed for day‑zero operators.
4) Telemetry & audit: audit log forwarding (SIEM) and retention policy agreed.
5) Smoke traffic: run the smoke test harness and confirm latency thresholds.

KMS notes: we support customer‑managed keys (AWS KMS / Google KMS). Required items: key ARN, grant policy, and proof of rotation schedule. For audit evidence we’ll need annual rotation policy and last‑rotation timestamp. We do not store KMS keys. Detailed KMS step‑by‑step is in tab 3 of the attached sheet.

Requested owner: can Aisha be the technical lead for the networking items? If yes, we’ll carve out a 60‑minute verification call next week (suggest Tuesday 10/3 or Wednesday 10/4 PST).

Next steps in the checklist: mark owners, attach your network diagram, and fill the preferred verification window.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_onprem_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 48 KB)

From: Aisha Rao <aisha@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy onboarding — preflight questions and timelines

Marcus, Ben — thanks. I’m happy to be the networking lead. Quick clarifications from our side after we reviewed the checklist and the attached answers: 

- Network diagram: attaching the current topology (acme_network_diagram_v1.png). We have a transit VPC, private subnets for workload, and a dedicated egress NAT. Ports and CIDR ranges are in the diagram notes.
- For smoke testing: do you provide a test harness or should we run sample traffic from our staging cluster to your endpoint?
- Compliance: we need a written statement for SOC2 evidence that logs will be retained for 365 days and exported to our SIEM. Where do we capture that in the process?

I filled in owner columns on the checklist and proposed the verification slot: Wednesday Nov 3, 09:00–10:00 PST.

Thanks —
Aisha Rao
Cloud Platform Lead, Acme Health
attachments: acme_network_diagram_v1.png (image/png, 245 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy onboarding — preflight questions and timelines

Aisha — good questions. Short answers and action items below. I’m copying the verification checklist steps so your infra team can map to tasks.

1) Smoke harness: Redwood will run the smoke harness from our validation env. We’ll provide a small test script for you to run from your staging (script: smoke_test_run.sh). Expect two passes: connectivity + functional token flow. For the connectivity pass we’ll validate:
   - TCP reachability on port 443 to the service endpoint
   - TLS certificate chain and SNI match
   - Source IP allowlist verification (we’ll provide expected egress IP set)

2) KMS & encryption verification: Steps we’ll run during verification call:
   - Confirm key ARN and policy
   - Run sample encrypt/decrypt via the attestation workflow (we’ll not store key material)
   - Confirm CloudTrail events for the KMS calls are visible in your account (or provide cross‑account viewing for audit)

3) Audit/logs: we will export request logs (redwood metadata) to your SIEM via the connector. We can confirm retention in the verification call and produce a short statement for SOC2 that lists export path and retention window.

4) Owners and timeline: I’ve added the following proposed schedule in the attached checklist:
   - Nov 3 — Technical verification call (60m)
   - Nov 10 — Pre‑go smoke pass (engineers on call)
   - Nov 18 — Soft go‑live

As follow‑ups, please share the egress NAT IPs (or allowlist your peer IPs) and a service account to test with (email: infra-testing@acmehealth.com). I’ll attach a short verification runbook after the call (no attachments yet — will send post‑call).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Thanks team — confirming the Nov 3 verification call at 09:00 PST. Request for meeting prep (short checklist to attach to calendar invite):

- Acme: network diagram (done), egress NAT IPs (please send reply to this thread), test service account + sample request tokens.
- Redwood: smoke_test_run.sh + expected egress IP list, verification runbook, short SOC2 export statement for logs (we’ll bring the document and update it with agreed retention).
- KMS: bring the KMS verification steps (Ben will run them live during the call).

If there are any blockers after the verification call we will escalate to the infra ops lead and aim to get the pre‑go smoke pass completed by Nov 10. Please reply to confirm owners and the IPs by EOD Monday Nov 1.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to the call.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
